Arkansas property tax is assessed and collected at the local level, and owners can appeal an assessment.

What the official sources say

  • The third Monday in August is the deadline to file an appeal with the county Board of Equalization. (Arkansas Assessment Coordination Division | DFA; source)
  • The assessment rate is 20% of true, actual, or market value (Ark. Code Ann. 26-26-303(c)). (Arkansas Property Tax FAQs (DFA); source)
  • Market value is determined as of the January 1 valuation date of the tax year. (Arkansas Property Tax FAQs (DFA); source)
  • Taxes are due from the first business day in March through October 15 of the year following the assessment year; a 10% penalty applies if not paid by then. (Arkansas Property Tax FAQs (DFA); source)
  • Amendment 79 caps annual increases in taxable value after reappraisal at 5% for homesteads and 10% for other real property, until full assessed value is reached. (Property Tax Relief | DFA; source)
  • At least 30 calendar days before an in-person tax-delinquent auction, the Commissioner of State Lands notifies the owner and interested parties by regular mail of the right to redeem. (26 CAR 400-106; source)
  • Redemption must be received before 4:00 p.m. CT on the last business day before the sale, by paying taxes, penalties, interest, fees, and costs. (26 CAR 400-106; source)

Arkansas Homestead Exemption: Eligibility, Filing and Selling the Home

Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Homeowners may receive a homestead property tax credit of up to $500 per year; beginning with 2026 tax bills the general assembly authorized an increase up to $600. (Property Tax Relief | DFA; source)
  • The homestead is the dwelling used as the principal place of residence; homeowners must apply for the credit with the county assessor's office. (Property Tax Relief | DFA; source)
  • Owners age 65 or older or disabled who qualify for the homestead credit may have the taxable assessed value of the homestead frozen; they must apply with the county assessor. (Property Tax Relief | DFA; source)
  • A freeze does not pass to a subsequent owner of the same home; a buyer cannot claim the seller's prior limitation. (Property Tax Relief | DFA; source)
  • The October 15 deadline applies to filing the Homestead Credit Application. (Arkansas Assessment Coordination Division | DFA; source)
  • Property owners may claim only one homestead tax credit each year. (Property Tax Relief | DFA; source)
Selling in Arkansas?
We buy Arkansas houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What is the Arkansas homestead tax credit worth now?

The credit is worth up to $675 a year on a qualifying home. The Assessment Coordination Division's 2026 annual report says it was raised from $600 by House Bill 1103 of 2026, and the Benton County and Washington County assessors both quote $675 on their public pages.

The state's property tax relief page still carries older wording, up to $500 and then up to $600 for 2026 tax bills. Treat the newer figure as the working number, and confirm it with your county assessor before you quote it to a buyer or a tax preparer.

The word exemption is common in everyday speech, but Arkansas gives a credit. Amendment 79, section 3, directs the General Assembly to provide an annual state credit against property tax on a homestead, and the credit cannot exceed the tax owed. The Benton County assessor gives an example: if the tax bill is $650, the credit pays $650 and nothing more, since the state does not send the difference.

Who qualifies, and where do you apply?

You qualify if the house is your principal place of residence and you hold the right kind of ownership interest. You apply with the county assessor's office where the house is located, as the Department of Finance and Administration states.

  • A record owner qualifies, and so does a buyer under a recorded sales contract or a person holding a recorded life estate.
  • The home may be held in a revocable or irrevocable trust.
  • A person who deeded the home away but kept a recorded life estate and still lives there can qualify.
  • A nursing home or retirement center resident who still owns the residence can qualify in some circumstances.
  • An LLC can qualify when it supplies a certificate of good standing and a member signs an attestation that the house is that member's primary residence and no other credit is claimed (Benton County assessor).

An owner may claim only one homestead credit per year. A landlord's rental house, a vacant inherited house and a second home do not meet the principal residence test.

Which Arkansas property tax breaks sit alongside the credit?

Amendment 79 produced three relief tools besides the credit: a freeze for owners 65 and older or disabled, a 5% yearly cap on homestead increases, and a 10% cap on other real property. The table sums them up.

BenefitWho gets itWhat it doesHow to get it
Homestead creditOwner-occupantsUp to $675 off the yearly tax billApply with the county assessor
Age 65 or disabled freezeHomestead owners who qualify for the creditFreezes the taxable assessed valueApply with the county assessor
Homestead capHomesteads after a reappraisalTaxable value rises 5% per year until it reaches full assessed valueApplied through the assessment
Cap on other real propertyCommercial, agricultural and vacant parcelsTaxable value rises 10% per year until full valueApplied through the assessment

The caps do not apply to newly discovered property, new construction or substantial improvements. Arkansas defines a substantial improvement as renovation, reconstruction and refurbishment that adds 25% or more to the value of the property.

Disabled veterans have a separate exemption. Act 407 of 2025 raised the contiguous land counted as the homestead for that exemption from 40 to 80 acres, effective for assessment years beginning on or after January 1, 2025.

How does the age 65 or disabled freeze work?

The freeze locks the taxable assessed value of the home at the next assessment date after you turn 65 or become disabled. It does not lock the tax bill. The Benton County assessor warns that a millage increase by a city, county or school district can still raise what you pay.

A person who is already 65 or disabled when buying a home can have the value frozen at the next assessment date after the purchase. The owner must apply, and the assessor asks for proof: a driver's license, state ID or birth certificate for age, or a Medicare card or Social Security award letter for disability, according to the Benton and Washington County pages.

Additions to the house can end the freeze. Benton County says the freeze is removed when a homeowner adds on and then reapplied at the new value.

What happens to the credit and the freeze when you sell?

Neither one travels with the house. The state says a freeze cannot pass to a later owner of the same home, and a buyer cannot claim the seller's earlier limitation.

The statute behind this is Ark. Code § 26-26-1123, which the Benton County assessor quotes. After a sale, the assessor values the property at 20% of its appraised value on the next assessment date following the transfer of title. The new owner cannot claim an assessment limitation until the second assessment date after the transfer. That is why a buyer's first tax bill can look sharply higher than the seller's last one.

Three steps are worth taking when you are the seller:

  • Tell the assessor when the house stops being your principal residence.
  • Do not expect a second credit. If you buy another home, the one-credit-per-year rule applies to you as an owner.
  • Settle at closing who pays the bill that arrives after the sale. Arkansas taxes are paid a year behind, so the 2026 assessment is billed in spring 2027 and due October 15, 2027, per the Benton County assessor.

Is the homestead tax credit the same as protection from creditors?

No. The tax credit lowers a property tax bill. Protection of a homestead from judgment creditors is a separate matter under Article 9 of the Arkansas Constitution.

An Arkansas court quoting Article 9, section 3 describes it this way: the homestead of a resident who is married or the head of a family is not subject to the lien of a judgment or to sale under execution, with exceptions the constitution lists. How that applies to a particular house, including one in bankruptcy, takes a lawyer's reading. Filing for the tax credit does not create or remove that protection.

How does the homestead credit fit into selling an Arkansas house for cash?

It matters most for the paperwork around the sale, since the credit ends with your ownership and the cash price does not change it.

Property taxes are due to the county collector by October 15 each year. Craighead County's collector says taxes unpaid after that date draw a 10% penalty, and Faulkner County's collector adds 10% annual interest on real estate taxes. Parcels that stay delinquent are certified to the Commissioner of State Lands, and title vests in the state, so a seller behind on taxes should clear the balance before listing or signing.

The deed carries its own tax. The Arkansas real property transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on transactions above $100, as the Department of Finance and Administration states, paid through a stamp on the deed.

More questions about Arkansas Homestead Exemption

Does Arkansas have a homestead exemption?

Arkansas offers a homestead property tax credit rather than an exemption of value. It is worth up to $675 a year on a principal residence, and owners 65 or older or disabled can also apply to freeze the taxable assessed value.

Where do I apply for the Arkansas homestead credit?

You apply with the county assessor's office in the county where the home sits. The Department of Finance and Administration says the assessor handles both the credit and the age 65 or disability freeze, so ask that office for the form and the filing window.

Does the buyer inherit my homestead credit when I sell?

No. The buyer must apply as a new owner. Under Ark. Code § 26-26-1123 the buyer cannot claim a limit on assessed value until the second assessment date after the transfer, and a freeze cannot pass to a later owner.

Can I claim the credit on a rental or second home?

No. The credit applies only to a homestead used as the owner's principal place of residence, and an owner may claim only one credit per year.

Will turning 65 stop my property taxes from rising?

No. The freeze holds the taxable assessed value, not the bill. If a city, county or school district raises its millage rate, your taxes can still go up.

Can a trust or an LLC get the credit?

A trust can, because the home may be held in a revocable or irrevocable trust. An LLC can too when it files a certificate of good standing and a signed member attestation that the house is that member's primary residence.

title: Arkansas Eviction Process and Selling a Rented House
content:
Arkansas Eviction Process and Selling a Rented House

Cash Home Buyers in Arkansas
Cash Offer in 24 Hours

  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Arkansas Eviction Process and Selling a Rented House sale
  • Turn the Arkansas Eviction Process and Selling a Rented House offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling a Arkansas House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the official sources say

  • Failure to pay rent, or to pay on time, is grounds for eviction; a landlord may bring a civil 'unlawful detainer' action. (Landlord And Tenant Rights | Arkansas AG; source)
  • After receiving a summons, the tenant has five days to object in writing to the clerk; without an objection the sheriff can remove the tenant, and with one a hearing is scheduled. (Landlord And Tenant Rights | Arkansas AG; source)
  • Property left in the dwelling at lease termination is considered abandoned and may be disposed of by the landlord. (Landlord And Tenant Rights | Arkansas AG; source)
Selling in Arkansas?
We buy Arkansas houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

How does an eviction work in Arkansas?

Arkansas gives a landlord three separate ways to get a tenant out: a civil lawsuit called unlawful detainer, a case under the Residential Landlord-Tenant Act of 2007, and a criminal charge for refusing to leave. Most owners start with one of the first two.

Unlawful detainer is defined in Ark. Code § 18-60-304. A person commits it by holding over after a lease ends, by refusing a written demand to leave, by failing to pay rent and then refusing to quit after three days' written notice, by letting the premises become unsafe or unhealthy, or by allowing a common nuisance. Legal Aid of Arkansas describes it as the most common type of eviction in the state.

The Landlord-Tenant Act route starts at § 18-17-901. A landlord or agent may file in district court when rent is not paid when due or demanded, when the term of occupancy has ended, or when the rental agreement has been broken. For a residential lease, rent that stays unpaid five days after the due date counts as legal notice that eviction proceedings can begin.

What notice periods apply to an Arkansas eviction?

The notice a landlord must give depends on the reason for ending the tenancy. The table lists each trigger found in the statutes and the state guidance.

SituationNotice or waiting periodWhere it comes from
Rent unpaid, unlawful detainerThree days' written notice to quit§ 18-60-304(3); Attorney General
Rent unpaid, Landlord-Tenant ActLandlord may terminate if rent is not paid within five days of the due date§ 18-17-701(b)
Other lease violationWritten notice with a termination date at least 14 days after receipt, if not fixed§ 18-17-701(a)
Week-to-week tenancyWritten notice at least 7 days before the end date§ 18-17-704(a)
Month-to-month tenancyWritten notice at least 30 days before the end date§ 18-17-704(b)
Criminal failure to vacateTen days' written notice to vacate§ 18-16-101(b)

Legal Aid of Arkansas summarizes the civil timing as at least three days for unpaid rent, at least 14 days for other violations, and at least one month to end a month-to-month tenancy. The Attorney General adds that a landlord may end a lease for any reason, giving one rental period's notice on an oral lease or notice under the terms of a written one.

The sources word these periods a little differently, so a landlord should match the notice to the lease and the statute that fits the facts.

What happens after the notice period ends?

If the tenant is still in the house, the landlord files a complaint with the court, and the case moves through a short series of steps.

  • Service. Legal Aid says the tenant must receive the summons and complaint through a process server or by certified mail.
  • Five days to object. The Attorney General says a tenant who receives a summons has five days to object in writing to the court clerk. Without an objection, the county sheriff can remove the tenant.
  • Order to vacate or show cause. Under the Landlord-Tenant Act, if the complaint carries an affidavit from someone with knowledge of the reason for eviction, the court issues an order to vacate or to appear and show cause within ten calendar days after service. A written answer counts as an appearance.
  • Hearing. If the tenant appears, the judge hears both sides. A judgment for the tenant lets the tenant stay until the tenancy ends by agreement or law, rent goes unpaid, or another eviction case succeeds (§ 18-17-908).
  • Writ of possession. If the landlord wins, the clerk issues a writ and the sheriff serves it. Legal Aid says the tenant then has 24 hours to leave. The sheriff carries out the writ under the procedure in § 18-60-310, as § 18-17-913 directs.

Each of these steps is a minimum. Court calendars set the hearing date, so no statute gives a fixed total number of days from notice to move-out.

What is the criminal failure to vacate charge?

It is a misdemeanor for a tenant who willfully refuses to leave after ten days' written notice from the landlord, the landlord's agent or the landlord's attorney. The rule is in Ark. Code § 18-16-101.

The same section says a renter who fails to pay rent when due forfeits the right to keep occupying the dwelling. On conviction the fine is between $1 and $25 per offense, and each day of willful holding over after the notice expires counts as a separate offense.

Can a landlord change the locks or shut off utilities?

No. Legal Aid of Arkansas states that a landlord needs a court order and a writ of possession carried out by the sheriff, and may not use self-help methods.

  • Changing the locks is a self-help eviction.
  • Removing the tenant's belongings, doors or windows is also self-help.
  • Shutting off water, power or other utilities is self-help as well.

Legal Aid adds an exception: the same acts may be lawful when the tenant has already moved out or the landlord reasonably believes the property is abandoned. A tenant who is locked out can sue for forcible entry, and the court may restore access and award damages, costs and attorney's fees. The landlord may counterclaim to evict in the same case, since a lockout alone does not give the tenant a right to stay when there is a legal ground for eviction.

What happens to belongings left in the house?

When a lease ends, voluntarily or not, the Attorney General says everything the tenant leaves behind is considered abandoned and the landlord may dispose of it as the landlord sees fit, without recourse by the tenant. Property left on the premises is also subject to a landlord's lien for sums the tenant agreed to pay.

Legal Aid describes the other situation. If law enforcement has to carry out the eviction, items the tenant cannot take are removed and stored at the tenant's expense. If the tenant moves out first and leaves things behind, the landlord can treat them as abandoned and throw them away or sell them.

Can a tenant withhold rent over repairs?

No. Section 18-17-502 says a tenant may not offset or withhold rent for an alleged or actual violation of the implied quality standards, and nothing in the chapter excuses a tenant from paying rent.

For leases entered into or renewed after November 1, 2021, the statute implies several basics: hot and cold running water, electricity, potable water, working sanitary sewer and plumbing, a functioning roof and building envelope, and heating and air conditioning if the home had them when the lease was signed. If the unit falls short, the tenant sends written notice. When rent is current and the landlord does not fix the problem within 30 calendar days, the tenant's sole remedy is to end the lease without penalty and receive back any recoverable security deposit.

The City of Little Rock adds its own minimum housing standards for privately owned rentals with two or more dwellings, including a safe roof that does not leak. Problems can be reported to the Department of Housing and Neighborhood Programs at 500 West Markham Street, Suite 120W, or (501) 371-6825.

What money can a landlord recover in an eviction?

A landlord can recover actual damages, obtain injunctive relief and get a judgment or eviction in circuit or district court without posting bond, according to § 18-17-701(c).

Attorney's fees are possible when the landlord is represented by a lawyer. They are available if nonpayment of rent is not in good faith, and for other willful noncompliance. On a holdover, § 18-17-704 allows fees when the tenant is not holding over in good faith. A willful violation can add up to three months of periodic rent or twice the actual damages, whichever is greater.

How does an eviction affect selling a rented house in Arkansas?

The sale and the eviction are two separate tracks. The statutes above control who has the right to possession. They do not say that a sale ends a tenancy, so the lease terms and a lawyer's advice should come before any promise to a buyer that the house will be vacant.

A few practical points tie the two together. A landlord may decline to renew a lease for any reason except discriminatory ones covered by the Fair Housing Act, according to Legal Aid. A month-to-month tenant must be given 30 days' written notice. A buyer who is purchasing a house for cash can be asked whether it will take the property with the tenant still inside, which avoids waiting on a court calendar.

Tax paperwork follows the sale too. The Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration says the real property transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration on transactions above $100, shown on the deed through a transfer stamp. The Assessment Coordination Division also asks owners to tell the assessor when a house changes from owner-occupied to rental, which matters because the homestead credit only applies to a principal residence.

More questions about Arkansas Eviction Process and Selling a Rented House

How long does an Arkansas eviction take?

The statutes set minimum waits and no fixed total. Notice runs from three days to 30 days, a tenant has five days to object, a show-cause order allows up to ten days to appear, and a tenant served with a writ has 24 hours according to Legal Aid. A contested case adds a hearing date set by the court.

Is eviction a crime in Arkansas?

Only the failure to vacate charge is criminal. Under § 18-16-101, a tenant who willfully stays after ten days' written notice commits a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of $1 to $25 per offense, and each day counts separately.

Can a landlord evict without going to court?

No. Legal Aid of Arkansas says a landlord needs a court order, and the sheriff carries out the writ of possession. Changing locks, removing doors or windows, or cutting utilities are illegal self-help methods unless the tenant has left or the property is reasonably believed abandoned.

Does a pending eviction stop me from selling the house?

Nothing in the statutes cited here bars a sale while a case is open. The lease and the buyer's terms decide what happens to the tenant, so ask an Arkansas attorney before you sign a contract that promises vacant possession.

Where can a tenant find free legal help with an eviction?

Legal Aid of Arkansas offers free help to tenants who qualify, and its number is 1-800-952-9243.

This guide covers what official sources say about Arkansas transfer on death deeds.

What the official sources say

  • Arkansas calls it a beneficiary deed (Ark. Code 18-12-608): a deed without current tangible consideration conveying an interest upon the owner's death that expressly states it does not take effect until death. (Act 243 of 2007; source)
  • It is valid only if executed and recorded before the owner's death in the county recorder's office where the property is located. (Act 243 of 2007; source)
  • It may be revoked at any time by the owner (or any executing owner if more than one). (Act 243 of 2007; source)
  • No legal or equitable interest vests in the grantee until the owner's death prior to revocation. (Act 570 of 2021; source)
  • The transfer is subject to existing encumbrances and to a DHS claim for reimbursement of federal or state benefits from the estate or the interest acquired by the grantee (under 20-76-436). (Act 570 of 2021; source)
  • Act 423 of 2021 amends Ark. Code 28-41-101(a): a distributee may collect and distribute a small estate without a personal representative when no petition for appointment is pending or granted. (Act 423 of 2021 (arkleg.state.ar.us); source)
  • Forty-five days must have elapsed since the decedent's death. (Act 423 of 2021; source)
  • Value of all property owned, less encumbrances, must not exceed $100,000; the homestead and spousal/minor-child statutory allowances are excluded from that calculation. (Act 423 of 2021; source)

Arkansas probate runs through the courts named in the sources below.

What the official sources say

  • Act 423 of 2021 amends Ark. Code 28-41-101(a): a distributee may collect and distribute a small estate without a personal representative when no petition for appointment is pending or granted. (Act 423 of 2021 (arkleg.state.ar.us); source)
  • Forty-five days must have elapsed since the decedent's death. (Act 423 of 2021; source)
  • Value of all property owned, less encumbrances, must not exceed $100,000; the homestead and spousal/minor-child statutory allowances are excluded from that calculation. (Act 423 of 2021; source)
  • A distributee files an affidavit with the probate clerk of the circuit court of the county of proper venue, including a legal description and valuation of any real property. (Act 423 of 2021; source)
  • The affidavit must state there are no unpaid claims and that any DHS benefits furnished have been reimbursed. (Act 423 of 2021; source)

This guide covers what official sources say about Arkansas tax on a house sale.

What the official sources say

  • Arkansas taxes 50% of net long-term capital gain: the Arkansas taxable amount equals line 7b multiplied by 50 percent. (AR1000D Capital Gains 2024 | DFA; source)
  • Net capital loss deduction is limited to $3,000 ($1,500 per taxpayer for filing status 4 or 5). (AR1000D Capital Gains 2024 | DFA; source)
  • Short-term capital gains are included in full in Arkansas taxable capital gain. (AR1000D Capital Gains 2024 | DFA; source)
